title: Curtice Brothers v. Catts — tomatoes and substitution
shortTitle: Curtice Brothers v. Catts — tomatoes and substitution
summary: A cannery’s time-sensitive supply need can make ordinary market damages inadequate.
notes:
Casebook discussion of a shorter authority.

The discussion concerns the need for enough tomatoes during a limited processing season, the feasibility of substitute purchases, and the practical possibility of supervising relief. It shows why plentiful ordinary goods can still present an inadequate-remedy problem in a particular transaction.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 28–30. Open assigned page 28.
